messages:
alex: Heads up — the Go SDK onboarding sample app's generator example is misbehaving with auth refresh. Repro: short-lived token + long streaming generator -> goroutine leaks after ctx cancel. Anyone seen this?

jamie: yep saw that during load test yesterday :grimace:

maria: I hit it too. Sample uses `context.Background()` inside the retry goroutine which ignores the parent request ctx. When the token refresh triggers a retry, the inner goroutine keeps running and writes to channels after the handler returns.

alex: minimal repro snippet I used:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
g, _ := client.NewGenerator(...)
stream, err := g.Stream(ctx, input) // stream spins off retry/backoff goroutines
if err != nil { return err }
for tok := range stream.Recv() { fmt.Println(tok) }
```
Problem is stream.Recv() never unblocks if inner goroutine is stuck.

sash: Oof. Two parts: API ergonomics (stream should expose ctx-aware Close/Cancel) and sampleapp using the wrong pattern. We should show the pattern of creating a child ctx bound to token TTL and propagate that into the retry handler.

jamie: Agreed. UX suggestion: Stream could return an object with `Done() <-chan struct{}` and `Close() error` so callers don't rely on reading the channel forever. Also document that retries must respect the caller's ctx.

maria: I'll draft a small API proposal: keep Stream(ctx, req) but change return to (*GeneratorStream, error). GeneratorStream has `Recv(ctx) (Chunk, error)` and `Close() error`. That makes cancellation explicit and avoids hidden goroutines.

alex: That sounds like a good compromise for backward compat: we can add a new method set and mark old streaming helpers deprecated in the next minor. Add a sample snippet showing usage.

maria: Sample usage I'll add to sampleapp:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(reqCtx, 10*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
go func() { <-ctx.Done(); stream.Close() }()
for {
  chunk, err := stream.Recv(ctx)
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { return err }
  fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
}
```
This ensures Close is called if the parent ctx cancels.

sash: Also add an e2e in CI that simulates auth refresh mid-stream (short TTL + forced refresh) so we catch regressions.

jamie: Can we also add a lint rule in the sampleapp repo to forbid `context.Background()` in long-lived goroutines? Might be heavy-handed but could catch common mistakes.

maria: I'll open a PR with code + tests + updated sample. Will include a small doc note about token-refresh patterns.

alex: awesome. Can you add a short blurb for the release notes and tag it for the next devex sprint? @dev-bot can you create a draft changelog entry when the PR lands?

dev-bot: Created draft changelog entry: "Go SDK: generator streaming - improve cancellation ergonomics and sample app token-refresh handling" (ID: CHG-4129) :white_check_mark:

maria: PR in progress, linking issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/issues/871 — I'll add the e2e that simulates refresh mid-stream.

ajex: thanks all, will follow up in PR review. :thumbsup:
